diff --git a/distribution/install.sh b/distribution/install.sh
index 331db68..752a1f3 100755
--- a/distribution/install.sh
+++ b/distribution/install.sh
@@ -135,7 +135,12 @@ trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"; [ -z "$tmp_out" ] || rm -f "$tmp_out"' EXIT
 # dies with its own sentence around that cause.
 fetch_url() { # $1 = URL, $2 = destination
 	fetch_error=""
+	# Send GITHUB_TOKEN when set, so users behind shared IPs get the
+	# authenticated rate limit instead of the anonymous one.
+	auth=""
+	[ -n "${GITHUB_TOKEN:-}" ] && auth="Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN"
 	status=$(curl --proto '=https' --proto-redir '=https' -sSL \
+		${auth:+-H "$auth"} \
 		-o "$2" -w '%{http_code}' "$1") || {
 		fetch_error="failed to fetch $1; check the connection and retry"
 		return 1

content.text:
The patch violates ADR-0585, which says `install.sh` must not read `GITHUB_TOKEN`. The patch reads it and sends it in an `Authorization` header. I did not read the repo files myself. The replay results below come from the precedent tool's replay of this patch.

- **Check 64** (`token set: no Authorization header anywhere (GITHUB_TOKEN never rides a request)`): the replay observed `not ok`, so it fails.
- **Check 7** (`drift guard: install.sh consults no GitHub API endpoint (ADR-0585)`): passes. The patch doesn't add an API endpoint.
- **Check 193** (`no case made a GitHub API request (ADR-0585)`): passes.
